ui_bugs.issue: STALE-CLOSURE BUG: Selecting a Movement Type does nothing on the FIRST change (API call fires with OLD filters). Captured network proof: click 'Fast Moving' -> GET /api/reports/inventory_material?tab=movement (NO movement_type query); then click 'Slow Moving' -> GET ...?movement_type=fast (one step behind). Root cause: setFilters is async and fetchReport(useCallback dep=[filters]) captures the previous filters in the same tick. Fix: pass value directly e.g. fetchReport(activeReport, activeTab, { movement_type: v }) OR move fetchReport into a useEffect on filters.movement_type.

rca of the issue: Movement filter bug RCA — `fetchReport` is a useCallback with dependency on [filters]. When the user changes the Select, the handler calls `setFilters(p => ({...p, movement_type: v}))` followed IMMEDIATELY by `fetchReport(...)`. Because React batches state updates, `fetchReport` in that exact call still closes over the PREVIOUS filters object (movement_type=old). The new filters value only takes effect on the next render, and `fetchReport` is not automatically re-invoked. Net effect: every selection acts one step behind. Reproduction: open Movement tab -> select Fast Moving -> /api/reports/inventory_material fires WITHOUT movement_type -> select Slow Moving -> fires WITH movement_type=fast. Fix: useEffect(() => { fetchReport(activeReport, activeTab) }, [filters.movement_type]) OR pass the fresh value explicitly to fetchReport.
